proposed_from.topic: Fixed-budget sparse graph-discovery and honest-inference frontier for adaptive network experiments. For even n and horizon T, observe the full outcome vector after each fixed-budget assignment Z_t with exactly B treated units, under the sparse additive interference model mu_i(z)=alpha_i+tau_i z_i+sum_{j!=i} beta_ij A_ij z_j, maximum degree s<=n/8, beta-min delta, bounded coefficients, and conditionally independent sub-Gaussian noise. Define R* as worst-case cumulative welfare regret minimized over legal sequential designs that also recover A with uniform error at most 1/T. Determine the sharp nonasymptotic order of R*, construct a polynomial-time balanced-pool adaptive design and decoder with simultaneous support certificates, and prove a matching lower bound over every recovery-valid design. For the attaining design, construct debiased martingale estimators with simultaneous support-selection-uniform terminal coverage for TATE and selected edge spillovers. Consumers are Yu et al.'s Instagram A/B interference-characterization workflow and Holtz et al.'s Airbnb pricing meta-experiment. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For a uniform B-subset assignment with p=B/n, the centered design covariance was derived as p(1-p)n/(n-1) times the projector orthogonal to the all-ones vector; every k-sparse contrast consequently has eigenvalue at least p(1-p)(n-k)/(n-1). Since differences of two legal row models are at most (2s+1)-sparse, 2s+1<n removes the exact-budget null direction. Exact enumeration found three B=4 pools distinguishing all 764 degree-at-most-one graphs at n=8. The legal matching witness, s=n/8 boundary, partial matchings, empty-versus-one-edge alternatives, arbitrary signs, welfare-score cancellation, sigma=0, delta=L, short horizons, and the close Wang et al. 2026 unknown-support regret paper were checked without a collision or counterexample. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove a matching change-of-measure lower bound for regret, rather than sample size alone, forced by sparse restricted excitation under adaptive fixed-cardinality actions and graph error at most 1/T, with the correct joint dependence on s, delta, sigma, L, and the top-B learning term. EARLY KILL TEST: Solve the s=1 matching subclass first and prove matching upper and lower bounds for its balanced-pool discovery-regret tax while retaining the top-B optimization term; failure to beat singleton-style n-round exploration or failure of the additive regret lower bound should pivot the run.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The two closest linear-recovery ancestors are WangWainwrightRamchandran2010 for support-recovery limits under sparse measurements and AldridgeJohnsonScarlett2016 for constant-weight pooling. The former independently sparsifies entries of a random measurement matrix; the latter fixes item degrees and observes Boolean OR outcomes. YangDraperNowak2016 is the closest graph-recovery comparator, but its passive CSMA/CA activations and ACK/NACK observations do not provide controlled exact-budget assignments or signed full-vector responses. None applies to a matrix whose every row has exactly \(B\) ones, whose centered columns sum to zero, and whose signed linear measurements are reused simultaneously across \(n\) causal outcome regressions. Relative to YuAiroldiBorgsChayes2022 and AgarwalAgarwalMasoeroWhitehouse2024, the contribution is not another total-effect or regret estimator: it is a necessary-and-sufficient graph-identification condition and a finite-sample certificate map for both present and absent directed edges. The exact minimax pool complexity is stated openly because the upper and lower bounds leave a genuine sparsity-dependent computational-statistical gap.

seed_details.anchor: GleichLaberVolfovsky2026, Theorems 2 and 3, their proofs, and the discussion of the remaining \(n\)-factor discovery gap
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace singleton isolation by a constant-weight column-separation lemma, then attach KaufmannCappeGarivier2016 likelihood accounting to actionwise welfare loss.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for fixed-cardinality support recovery with full-vector signed responses and regret located constant-weight group testing and combinatorial pure exploration separately, but no theorem joining them.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is immediate from the anchor's partial-matching lower bound because its hard instance already consists of disjoint pairs.
seed_details.rebuttal: The anchor permits singleton actions and prices only a linear information lower bound; it neither constructs balanced pools nor proves the exact-\(B\) entropy-excitation tax or its additive welfare converse.

seed_details.seed: Exact-budget signed-support sample complexity and certificates
seed_details.anchor: YuAiroldiBorgsChayes2022, Theorem 1, Theorem 2, and the conclusion on avoiding costly network measurement
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's network-free unbiasedness construction by a necessary-and-sufficient sparse excitation condition on constant-weight treatment columns.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found Boolean constant-weight group testing and nonadaptive debiased-lasso maxima, but no signed additive-network decoder with exact-cardinality pools and simultaneous inclusion and exclusion certificates.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Ordinary compressed sensing already recovers each sparse row once a restricted eigenvalue holds.
seed_details.rebuttal: The legal designs lie in an affine exact-budget slice, the same pools serve all rows, the coefficients have arbitrary signs, and the claim includes a sharp pool count plus network-wide exclusion certificates.

seed_details.anchor: WangHongLiLiZhangWang2025, Theorems 4.1 and 5.6 and the proof's two-environment Le Cam reduction
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Add alternative-wise graph-support testing constraints to the anchor's reward-versus-interval-width allocation inequality.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found adaptive policy-value intervals and online high-dimensional debiasing, but not a three-resource frontier with exact graph recovery and randomly selected edge targets.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The third coordinate is just forced exploration appended to the published regret-inference frontier.
seed_details.rebuttal: Graph discrimination and score precision use different sparse directions under exact-budget covariance, so the joint attainable region need not be a scalar exploration-floor reparameterization.

seed_details.anchor: GleichLaberVolfovsky2026, the general-network explore-then-commit theorem and conclusion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the anchor's edge-by-edge exploration schedule by a degree-\(s\) sparse-switching packing and an oracle-implementable reward-information allocation.
seed_details.destination_search: HaoLattimoreWang2020 gives sparse information-regret packings without constant-weight network actions; the searched network-bandit papers do not require uniform graph recovery.
seed_details.cynical_objection: This is a routine sparsity substitution in the anchor's \(n^2\)-round analysis.
seed_details.rebuttal: The missing object is a joint adaptive welfare converse over legal fixed-cardinality actions, not a replacement of \(n\) by \(s\) in an upper bound.

seed_details.anchor: GleichLaberVolfovsky2026, downstream causal-analysis section and conclusion
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Upgrade the anchor's root-mean-square evaluation to a predictable debiasing expansion whose maximum ranges over the graph selected from the same filtration.
seed_details.destination_search: DeshpandeJavanmardMehrabi2023 treats adaptive coordinates and ZhangCheng2017 treats nonadaptive maxima, but the exact target-method pair was not located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Sample splitting followed by the ordinary debiased lasso solves the selection problem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sample splitting sacrifices the same-path terminal target and does not establish uniform validity over adaptive exact-budget branches with random realized excitation.

seed_details.seed: Entropy-to-excitation phase transition for balanced pools
seed_details.anchor: Prior proposal exp-rollout-common-uniform-covariance-design, degree-one exactness and Vandermonde-rank proof fields
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace distinct rollout probabilities and the Vandermonde argument by column entropy and sparse restricted eigenvalues inside one exact-cardinality slice.
seed_details.destination_search: AldridgeJohnsonScarlett2019 covers constant-weight Boolean pooling, but not the necessary-and-sufficient frontier for signed shared full-vector regressions.
seed_details.cynical_objection: The covariance projector makes the result an elementary restricted-eigenvalue corollary.
seed_details.rebuttal: The projector supplies only population excitation; the finite pool count must simultaneously meet an entropy lower bound, uniform row separation, noise robustness, and a polynomial construction.

seed_details.anchor: HoltzLobelLiskovichAral2024, meta-experiment results and discussion of the clustering-quality trade-off
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace a known-graph cluster objective by its supremum over a simultaneous edge-support confidence set and certify the rounded design's robust gap.
seed_details.destination_search: UganderYin2023 and EichhornKhanUganderYu2024 optimize or analyze supplied designs and graphs; no robust optimization over a learned graph certificate was located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Robustifying the known-graph objective is a standard worst-case optimization exercise.
seed_details.rebuttal: Missed and false edges change exposure probabilities discontinuously, so tractability and uniform design-based coverage require a new certificate-compatible relaxation.

seed_details.anchor: GleichLaberVolfovsky2026, modular-collapse theorem reducing total welfare to latent unit scores
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Characterize the null space of aggregate welfare feedback and prove exactly which additional row-wise outcome contrasts identify the graph without changing policy value.
seed_details.destination_search: The searched interference-policy papers exploit aggregate reward or full outcomes, but no exact equivalence frontier between welfare sufficiency and graph identifiability was located.
seed_details.cynical_objection: Summing the additive outcome equation already gives the score decomposition.
seed_details.rebuttal: The nontrivial half is the iff boundary identifying which observation operators recover support while leaving all welfare functionals observationally equivalent.

seed_details.seed: Computational regret for approximate posterior sampling
seed_details.anchor: GleichLaberVolfovsky2026, modular Thompson-sampling theorem and the stated open mixing-time problem for the Gibbs approximation
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact posterior draws in the modular regret proof by a quantitative total-variation perturbation accumulated from a graph-posterior Gibbs chain.
seed_details.destination_search: Approximate Thompson-sampling analyses were found in generic bandits, but not for the anchor's joint graph-and-policy posterior with sparse interference.
seed_details.cynical_objection: A standard approximate-posterior regret perturbation immediately applies.
seed_details.rebuttal: The graph posterior is multimodal and its mixing error is policy-dependent; a usable theorem needs a structural conductance bound rather than an assumed approximation tolerance.
